evals.prompt: Audit an account where team lookup succeeds but policies/routes return empty arrays. The owner says paging should already be configured.
evals.expected_output: Record the complete empty census; block expected paging-path checks. Do not infer every item schema, report a healthy100, create fixtures or swap to the setup key.

evals.prompt: A routed rotation has five time periods and a current block, but shiftMembers is empty and scheduled-user is JSONnull. An unrelated unused rotation has the same shape.
evals.expected_output: Treat periods as time windows only. Report the referenced unstaffed shift with exact consequence; keep the unused empty rotation informational. No future outage duration or device-delivery claim.

evals.prompt: Two routing targets resolve to two policies and the same enrolled user. The operator explicitly requires two independent responders. There are also three pending invitations.
evals.expected_output: Deduplicate enrolled current users, count one responder, ignore pending invitations as coverage, and flag the declared redundancy gap with both policies and a verification step.

evals.prompt: Select team alpha in an account with a fanout route to alpha and beta. The routing response includes a key, apiKey in an unknown nested field, and provider self URLs. A label override is misspelled.
evals.expected_output: Reject the unknown label before a network call. With a valid label, project before writing, drop secrets/URLs, retain outside-policy scope metadata, and never call the beta target missing or equate route ordinals across batches.

evals.prompt: The first team read is correct; subsequent current data returns onCallNow/onCallUser, then a repeated identity read changes the team slug. Another probe gets HTML200 or429.
evals.expected_output: Stop on schema/identity/transport failure. Do not coerce casing, turn denied data into empty arrays, follow redirects or make a write to test permissions. Preserve safe completed evidence only.

evals.prompt: An upstream monitor contains a VictorOps handle but no exact secret-key mapping. A previous provider test incident is RESOLVED while the source is still firing.
evals.expected_output: Block the source join until exact source-side proof exists. Do not strip a handle prefix to invent a key. Describe provider resolution as cleanup and preserve the firing source; never claim recovery or measured incident statistics.

evals.prompt: Two configured On-Call accounts share the same route key, policy and team slugs. A source capture from the first target is replayed after selecting the second. A source batch also contains handle-only records and missing declared mappings.
evals.expected_output: Reject the target or credential-generation replay before provider reads. Require the versioned source capture, receipt and private exact-value binding. Collect one fresh management snapshot for all selected source records, retain candidates and missing mappings in the blocked denominator, and never treat a handle as an exact key or path counts as incidents. Legacy evidence remains readable but cannot certify a new SOC-007 result.
